title: Mirabai
hook: a princess ties bells to her ankles and dances in public, and people call her mad

segments.voice: Yesterday, Andal's dream of a wedding: a thousand elephants, and a bride who walked into the shrine. Today, a princess with bells on her feet.

Small brass bells, strung on a cord and tied around the ankles. Every step rings. You can't sneak anywhere wearing them; that's rather the point. Dancers wear them on stage. In one of the songs sung in her name, a princess ties them on and dances, in public, for Krishna. The town talks. Her husband's family is mortified. And the song hides none of it. It repeats what people said about her, and then it shrugs. Year three heard Mira's poison cup and her treasure. Today, her feet.
screen: `BELLS TIED AROUND THE ANKLES.` → `THE TOWN TALKS.` → `TODAY, HER FEET.`

segments.voice: The song opens with the line people know it by, pag ghunghroo bandh Mira nachi re. The sense, in paraphrase: Mira tied bells on her feet and danced. I've made myself my Lord's own servant. People say Mira's gone mad. My mother-in-law says I've ruined the family. And the last line: Mira's Lord is Giridhar, and she has met the undying one with ease. First, who's speaking about her. The people, the mother-in-law, the family: the song lets them all have their say. It doesn't argue back. It just goes on dancing. The mother-in-law's word, ruin of the family, shows the line a royal woman crossed by dancing in the open, and the song names it. Second, the word for mad there is bawari, and in Mira's songs madness isn't only an insult. In another song she calls herself prem diwani, mad with love. So the charge the town throws at her becomes something she wears, like the bells. Third, the bells make devotion something you can hear. Bhakti, the way of loving devotion, isn't only a feeling in the chest. In Mira's songs it moves the feet, keeps a rhythm, gathers a crowd. These songs are still sung with a drum and cymbals, in temples and living rooms, and sometimes danced. A song about a woman who wouldn't keep still is very hard to sing sitting still.
screen: `MIRA TIED BELLS ON HER FEET` · `THE TOWN HAS ITS SAY` · `MAD, THE WORD SHE WEARS` · `DEVOTION YOU CAN HEAR`

segments.voice: Let one hand tap your knee very softly, in time with the breath: in, one tap; out, one tap. After a few rounds, let the hand rest and keep the beat inside, just in the breath. If you pray, you can let the name you love ride that rhythm.
Mirabai. In one of her songs she ties bells on her ankles and dances for Krishna, and when the town calls her mad, she takes the word as her own.
Your line: Mirabai. Her devotion had a sound, and the whole town heard it. See you tomorrow.

original.note: Hindi. -bai is a respectful ending for a woman's name in western India; the songs mostly call her simply Mira.
